_comment: Single source of truth for pipeline gate steps. All guards + pipeline-mark-done.sh read this via pipeline-lib.sh. To add/remove a required gate step, edit ONLY this file.
_comment_order: The gates arrays ARE the step order: a step's position decides who is downstream of it. Only a step with a later content-bound step in the same gate can be bound to the round instead of the content.
_comment_binding: content (default, applies to anything not listed) = the marker's staged_hash must equal the current staged hash. round = the marker also counts when it was written in the SAME round (same HEAD, within 24h, has staged_tree, drift under round_drift) and some LATER content-bound step vouches for the final content. simplify is round-bound because review sits after it and does look at the final content; document_release / tidy_docs are last in gates.ship, so nobody is downstream of them and they stay content-bound.
_comment_drift: round_drift caps how much content a round-bound step never saw: added lines between its staged_tree and the current staged content. limit = min(max(floor_lines, ratio_percent% of the staged diff), max_lines). Calibrated 2026-09-20 on real sessions: observed review-phase edits had a median of ~29 lines and a p90 of ~136, and the one 390-line case is exactly what should force a simplify re-run.
_comment_exclude: exclude_paths are git pathspecs left out of both drift numbers, for files a house rule says to update in the same commit as the code (the TODO ledger, the verification docs) — counting them would let the ledger itself force a simplify re-run. Keep it narrow: a blanket *.md was the first version and it blinded the gate to repos whose product IS markdown (this one: SKILL.md, plugin READMEs).
_comment_evidence_gates: Which gates run pipeline_check_evidence. commit only, matching what the guards did before they shared one entry point — /ship never ran it, and switching that on as a side effect of a refactor would be an unrequested tightening. Listed here rather than defaulted in the shell: a list that lives only in code is exactly what the exclude_paths fallback got wrong. An unreadable or non-array value runs the check (strict), so a broken config cannot quietly widen the gate.
_comment_docs_only: Every staged path in `paths` and none in `instruction_paths` (for a gate listed in `gates`) → the commit gate is skipped entirely, no markers needed, AND the evidence hard-check is skipped with it (otherwise `fix(docs): typo` would still demand a regression test). An empty staged diff is never exempt. Separate from round_drift.exclude_paths, which only asks whether lines count toward drift. Full rationale — why not the old `^docs/` prefix, why instruction markdown is code, why instruction_paths uses :(glob,icase) (one pattern covers top-level AND nested; icase because macOS treats Claude.md and CLAUDE.md as the same file while git pathspec does not), why /ship stays strict — in README §純文件免審.
